description: Combine structures to solve real problems — and talk through them like an engineer.

screens.body: Nobody asks you to 'implement a stack' at work. They ask you to check parentheses, build undo, or serve customers in order — and the answer is always a combination: the right structure + the right algorithm + Big O awareness. This topic is the combo move.
screens.heading: Real problems are combos
screens.keyPoint: Structures + algorithms + Big O = real solutions.

screens.body: Is '(()())' balanced? Scan left to right with a stack: push every '('; on ')', pop. If you ever pop an empty stack — unbalanced. End with a non-empty stack — unbalanced. Empty at the end — balanced. A stack is perfect because the LAST opened paren must close FIRST.

check.question: For balanced parens, when you see ')', you…

screens.heading: Example: balanced parentheses

screens.body: Every text editor's undo is a stack of states. Type something → push the state. Hit undo → pop back to the previous state. Redo? That's a second stack. Two stacks, one feature you use every day.
screens.heading: Example: undo

screens.body: Printer jobs, customer support tickets, playlists — first come, first served. That's a queue: enqueue at the back, dequeue from the front. Using a stack here would serve the LAST arrival first — wrong tool, wrong order.
screens.heading: Example: serving a line

screens.body: Three questions, ten seconds: 1) What order do I need — LIFO, FIFO, or random access? 2) What operations must be fast? 3) How big is the data? Answer those and the structure picks itself. This is the thought process interviewers want to HEAR.

options: What did I use last time?
check.question: First question when choosing a structure:

screens.heading: Choosing under pressure
screens.keyPoint: Order, operations, size — then the structure picks itself.

screens.body: Picked a structure? Now name its costs, like you learned: array-backed stack push is O(1); queue-via-shift is O(n) per dequeue. Saying 'I'd use a stack — push and pop are O(1)' in an interview is a complete, strong answer.

options: The structure and its Big O
check.question: A strong answer includes…

screens.heading: Don't forget the Big O
screens.keyPoint: Name the structure AND its Big O.

screens.body: Interviewers score your thinking, not just your code. Narrate: 'I need LIFO order, so a stack. Push is O(1), pop is O(1). Edge case: popping an empty stack.' That's it — structure, costs, edge cases. Practice saying it about YOUR SwiftGigs code too.

screens.keyPoint: Structure, costs, edge cases — out loud.
